forces.title: EU policy drives geothermal adoption for heating and sovereignty
forces.description: The European Commission's Heating and Cooling Strategy for 2026 actively promotes geothermal energy, alongside industrial waste heat recovery and biomass cogeneration, as a key renewable heat source. This policy, part of the broader Affordable Energy Action Plan, aims to integrate local heat planning and reduce the EU's heavy reliance (70%) on fossil fuels like natural gas for heating and cooling. This regulatory support acts as a strong tailwind, encouraging investment and deployment of geothermal solutions to enhance energy sovereignty and system resilience across Europe.
forces.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

forces.title: Scaling deep geothermal as next-gen flexible power technology
forces.description: European utilities are increasingly focusing on a 'Tech-scaling enabler play' as one of four strategic responses to industry shifts. This involves enabling next-generation technologies, including deep geothermal, to reach deployable scale. The move aims to secure firm, sovereign, and flexible power options in response to market volatility and capital intensity. Partnering with OEMs, EPCs, and governments to derisk projects and accelerate deployment of such advanced technologies positions deep geothermal as a crucial upside driver for future energy supply and grid flexibility.
forces.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

viewpoints.title: EU policy supports geothermal for heating to enhance energy sovereignty
viewpoints.description: The European Commission's 2026 Heating and Cooling Strategy, part of the Affordable Energy Action Plan and Clean Industrial Deal, aims to modernize local heat planning. This includes significant support for geothermal energy, alongside industrial waste heat recovery and other renewable heat sources. This initiative is crucial for strengthening Europe's energy sovereignty by reducing its 70% reliance on fossil fuels, mainly natural gas, in the heating and cooling sector. The policy shift indicates a positive outlook for geothermal energy's role in diversified and localized heat networks.
viewpoints.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

demand_drivers.description: Europe's efforts to reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels, particularly natural gas, for heating and cooling are driving demand for domestic renewable sources like geothermal energy.
The heating and cooling sector accounts for nearly half of the EU's energy consumption and is 70% reliant on fossil fuels. Geothermal energy is a key solution to decarbonize this sector.
New strategies encourage modernizing district heating and integrating various local renewable heat sources, including geothermal, into circular energy systems.

new_opportunities.description: Geothermal energy can be integrated into modernized district heating networks, turning local resources into dispatchable heat and power.
Geothermal energy can be part of circular energy systems alongside waste-to-energy and biomass cogeneration, utilizing local waste streams and byproducts.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of demand drivers and new opportunities for geothermal energy within the context of the European Union's heating and cooling sector, as outlined in the European Commission's 2026 Heating and Cooling Strategy. No explicit market size or value provided.
